title: Follow the street art down Hosier Lane and AC/DC Lane
description: Melbourne's bluestone laneways repaint themselves constantly - Hosier, Rutledge, AC/DC and Centre Place, with coffee at every turn.

title: Meet under the big screen at Federation Square
description: Melbourne's divisive sandstone-and-zinc civic square, and the front door to ACMI and the Ian Potter Centre.

title: Do a winter night market lap of Queen Victoria Market
description: Seven hectares of open-air market trading since 1878, with a hot-food night market in winter and again in summer.

title: Stand under the stained-glass ceiling at NGV International
description: The oldest and most visited gallery in Australia - walk through the water wall and lie on the floor under Leonard French's ceiling.

title: See Phar Lap at the Melbourne Museum
description: Home to the mounted hide of Phar Lap, a living forest gallery and the Bunjilaka Aboriginal Cultural Centre.

title: Walk the treetop gorilla trail at Melbourne Zoo
description: Australia's oldest zoo, ten minutes from the city by tram, with summer twilight concerts on the lawn.

title: Stand in the penguin snow room at SEA LIFE Melbourne
description: A city-centre aquarium on the Yarra with king and gentoo penguins in a genuinely cold sub-Antarctic enclosure.

title: Do the Aboriginal Heritage Walk at the Royal Botanic Gardens
description: 38 hectares beside the Yarra, with a guided walk led by an Aboriginal guide through plants used on Kulin country.

title: Watch the little penguins come home at the St Kilda breakwater
description: A wild little penguin colony living in the rocks of the pier breakwater, ten minutes from the CBD and completely free.

title: Ride the Scenic Railway through Luna Park's giant mouth
description: Open since 1912, and its Scenic Railway is the oldest continually operating rollercoaster in the world - still with a brakeman riding along.

title: Photograph the 82 Brighton Bathing Boxes
description: A row of Victorian-era timber boxes on Dendy Street Beach, each individually owned, painted and worth more than a house in some towns.

title: Row a boat or kayak the Yarra through the city
description: Paddling the Yarra puts you below the skyline and the Boathouse Drive rowing sheds - a different city from the one on the bank.

title: Ride Puffing Billy with your legs over the side
description: An 1900 narrow-gauge steam railway through the Dandenongs - the one train where sitting on the windowsill is the point.

title: Walk the 1,000 Steps Kokoda Track Memorial Walk
description: A steep climb through mountain ash and tree ferns, built as a memorial to the Kokoda campaign.

title: See a platypus up close at Healesville Sanctuary
description: An all-Australian-species sanctuary in the Yarra Valley bush, with a platypus enclosure and a free-flight raptor show.

title: Float over the Yarra Valley in a dawn hot air balloon
description: Balloons lift at first light over Victoria's cool-climate Chardonnay and Pinot country, landing in time for a winery breakfast.

title: Get lost in the Arthurs Seat maze on the Mornington Peninsula
description: An hour from Melbourne - a hook of vineyards, hot springs, calm bay beaches and surf coast on the other side.

title: Catch the Sorrento to Queenscliff ferry across the Heads
description: A 40-minute crossing of the Rip that saves a three-hour drive, with dolphins alongside more often than not.

title: Walk out to Fort Nepean where Australia fired the first shot of WWI
description: Gun emplacements and tunnels at the very tip of the peninsula, which fired on a German steamer hours after war was declared in 1914.

title: Sit in the hilltop pool at Peninsula Hot Springs after dark
description: Geothermal water piped into more than 70 pools - the hilltop bath at night, in winter, is the one everybody remembers.

title: Do a lap of the Phillip Island Grand Prix Circuit
description: You can ride the circuit as a hot-lap passenger or drive a go-kart replica of one of the great MotoGP tracks.

title: Sit on the sand for the Penguin Parade
description: Hundreds of little penguins surf in at dusk and walk up the beach past you - book, and dress far warmer than you think.

title: Walk the boardwalk over the blowhole at the Nobbies
description: The western tip of Phillip Island, above Australia's largest fur seal colony out on Seal Rocks.

title: Watch the working sheepdogs on Churchill Island
description: The site of the first European crop planted in Victoria, now a heritage farm with daily whip-cracking and dog demonstrations.

title: Spend a weekend at Wilsons Promontory, the mainland's southern tip
description: Granite headlands, wombats on the roads and some of the whitest sand in the country - book Tidal River months in advance.

title: Hear the sand squeak underfoot at Squeaky Beach
description: Rounded quartz grains that genuinely squeak when you walk on them, between orange granite boulders.

title: Camp at Tidal River and watch the wombats come out
description: The Prom's only campground, on a tannin-stained river behind Norman Beach - ballot-allocated over summer.

title: Climb Mount Oberon for sunset over the Prom
description: A 6.8km return climb on a management vehicle track to a 360-degree view over the whole peninsula and its islands.

title: Drive the Great Ocean Road end to end
description: 243km built by returned WWI soldiers as the world's largest war memorial - do it west to east so you are on the ocean side.

title: Watch sunrise at the Twelve Apostles before the buses arrive
description: Limestone stacks left behind as the cliffs eroded - there are eight standing now, and dawn is the only quiet hour.

title: Walk down into Loch Ard Gorge
description: Named for an 1878 wreck from which only two teenagers survived, washing into this narrow beach between the cliffs.

title: Stand on the beach beneath the cliffs at Gibson Steps
description: 86 steps cut into the cliff face let you stand at the base of the stacks - the only place you see them from below. Check the tide.

title: Spot glow worms and wild koalas in the Otways
description: Cool temperate rainforest of myrtle beech and tree ferns behind the coast, with the country's most reliable wild koala spotting near Kennett River.

title: Walk the Maits Rest rainforest boardwalk
description: A 30-minute loop among 300-year-old myrtle beech and hollow mountain ash - the easiest genuine rainforest walk in Victoria.

title: Walk to Erskine Falls behind Lorne
description: A 30m waterfall in fern gully ten minutes inland from the Great Ocean Road's most popular beach town.

title: Eat fish straight off the boat at Apollo Bay harbour
description: A working fishing harbour where the co-op sells the catch, between the Otway hills and the sea.

title: Explore Gariwerd, the Grampians
description: Sandstone ranges rising out of flat farmland, holding the largest concentration of Aboriginal rock art in southern Australia.

title: Descend to the base of MacKenzie Falls
description: One of the few Victorian falls that runs all year - a steep staircase down to the spray at the bottom, and a hard climb back.

title: Squeeze through the Grand Canyon to The Pinnacle
description: A scramble through slot canyons and boulder tunnels to a railed rock platform hanging over the Halls Gap valley.

title: Watch the kangaroos take over Halls Gap at dusk
description: The Grampians' base town, where mobs of eastern grey kangaroos graze the oval and caravan park every evening.

title: Pan for real gold at Ballarat
description: The heart of the 1850s gold rush and the Eureka Stockade, with grand streetscapes built on the proceeds.

title: Watch the gold pour at Sovereign Hill
description: A full-scale working 1850s goldfields town where they pour a real gold ingot daily and you can go down a mine shaft.

title: Ride the vintage talking tram through Bendigo
description: Gold-boom architecture on a scale that seems absurd for the town's size, plus the Central Deborah Mine 61m underground.

title: Catch a blockbuster exhibition at Bendigo Art Gallery
description: One of Australia's oldest regional galleries, which regularly lands international fashion and design exhibitions no other regional city gets.

title: Board a working paddle steamer at Echuca wharf
description: The largest collection of operating paddle steamers in the world, at a red gum wharf built when this was Australia's busiest inland port.

title: Hire a houseboat on the Murray for a few nights
description: Australia's longest river, lined with river red gums - you drive the boat yourself and tie up to the bank wherever you like.

title: See the night sound-and-light show at Swan Hill Pioneer Settlement
description: A recreated river port town, with an after-dark laser show projected across the settlement and the Murray.

title: Taste 100-year-old Muscat in Rutherglen
description: Fortified wine country - Rutherglen Muscat and Topaque are among the very few wine styles Australia genuinely leads the world in.

title: Stand in Ned Kelly's cell at the Beechworth Gaol
description: An almost perfectly preserved gold town where the Kelly family were repeatedly tried - plus a very good bakery and brewery.

title: Walk under the autumn trees in Bright
description: An alpine town planted with elms, oaks and maples that turns spectacular for about three weeks every April.

title: Walk out to the Horn on Mount Buffalo
description: A granite plateau of tors, snow gums and the Gorge - Victoria's oldest alpine park and much quieter than the ski resorts.

title: Ski or snowshoe at Falls Creek
description: Victoria's largest alpine resort, ski-in ski-out, and in summer one of the best mountain biking areas in the country.

title: Drive the Great Alpine Road over Mount Hotham
description: The highest year-round sealed road in Australia, running along a ridgeline through snow gum country.

title: Take the waters at Daylesford
description: The centre of Australia's largest concentration of mineral springs, and a weekend town of bathhouses, bakeries and Lake Daylesford.

title: Pump your own mineral water at Hepburn Springs
description: Free public hand pumps in the Mineral Springs Reserve - bring a bottle and taste the difference between each spring.

title: See a show at the Castlemaine Theatre Royal
description: A goldfields town turned arts town, with one of the oldest continuously operating theatres on the Australian mainland.

title: Stand inside the Great Stupa of Universal Compassion
description: A 50m Tibetan Buddhist stupa rising out of the bush near Bendigo, holding the Jade Buddha for Universal Peace.

title: Take a boat out to Skull Rock off Wilsons Promontory
description: Cleft Island - a granite dome with a 130m cave mouth like an eye socket, reachable only by boat on a calm day.

title: Wander the Dimboola Imaginarium
description: A gloriously strange gallery, curiosity shop and cafe in a tiny Wimmera town most people only see from the highway.

title: Photograph the Giant Koala at Dadswells Bridge
description: A 14m concrete koala on the Western Highway, and a properly good entry in Australia's Big Things canon.

title: Tick off the Big Wine Bottle at Rutherglen
description: A converted water tower painted as a giant bottle - the Big Thing that marks the entrance to fortified wine country.

title: Cross the Murray from Wodonga into New South Wales on foot
description: The Victorian half of the Albury-Wodonga border twin towns - you can walk over the river and change states mid-bridge.

title: Walk the Griffiths Island lighthouse loop at Port Fairy
description: A whitewashed fishing village at the quiet end of the coast, with a short-tailed shearwater colony on the island each summer.

title: Walk into a dormant volcano at Tower Hill
description: A nest of volcanic cones inside a crater lake, replanted from a Eugene von Guerard painting and now full of emus and koalas.

title: Kayak the Mallacoota inlet
description: A remote town at the far eastern corner of Victoria, on a huge quiet inlet between Croajingolong wilderness and the sea.

title: Sail the Gippsland Lakes and cross to Ninety Mile Beach
description: The largest inland waterway network in Australia, separated from the ocean by a single long dune of Ninety Mile Beach.
